sources.citation: Quebec retailer listing only, checked: 2026-07-31. No vendor protocol document names this product.

transport: Presumed two independent devices behind one faceplate: the inverter/charger on VE.Bus (which would put it on victron-vebus-mk2 or victron-gx-modbus-vebus) and the charge controller on VE.Direct or VE.Can (which would put it on victron-vedirect-text / victron-mppt-vedirect-hex). Neither assignment is attested. Nothing is claimed about baud, addressing or framing.

sharedMapEvidence: None. dialect: unknown, deliberately. An EasySolar (first generation) is a MultiPlus, a BlueSolar MPPT and an AC distribution board in one enclosure, and by construction the Multi part sits on VE.Bus and the MPPT part on its own port — but NO committed Victron document names "EasySolar" anywhere. The MK2 protocol's supported-devices list names Phoenix Multi, Phoenix Inverter and Quattro. The data-
gotchas: Do not fold these two models into victron-vebus-mk2 on the strength of the word "MultiPlus" in a marketing description. That is precisely the "same vendor, same family name" reasoning the catalogue forbids.

The retailer's only protocol claim is "Color Control (GX) integration", which if true routes to victron-gx-modbus-vebus for the inverter half and to the solar-charger service for the MPPT half — two dialects, two unit IDs, one box. A driver author who expects one device will be surprised.

The MPPT inside the 48/5000 is a 150/100. Four BlueSolar models are PV-only (no communication without sun) per rev 18, and 0xA047 BlueSolar MPPT 150/100 is NOT among them — but which PID the integrated unit reports is unknown, so even that is not settled.

What would settle it: a Victron document naming EasySolar (first generation) against a VE.Bus port or against com.victronenergy.vebus, or a bench capture of the PIDs the two internal devices report on a GX. Neither exists in this sweep.
